pr_title: *: fix bug of same type plans with different plan digest
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: crazycs520 <crazycs520@gmail.com>

<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/19516.

### What is changed and how it works?

The cause of same type plan with different digest is:

1. The Plan ID of plan may be changed, we should ignore the plan ID when normalized plan.
2. The Column Unique ID maybe also changed, we should also ignore the column unique id when normalized column info.
3. Fix the `PhysicalIndexScan` implementation of `PhysicalIndexJoin`, `PhysicalTableReader `, `PhysicalIndexScan ` , `basePhysicalAgg`.

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test

Side effects

- No

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- Fix issue of same type plans with different plan digest.

issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

1. Run [TPCC test](https://docs.pingcap.com/zh/tidb/stable/benchmark-tidb-using-tpcc) to reproduce.
2. Check the `information.STATEMENTS_SUMMARY` system check, here is an example:

 Plan 1:

```log
              PLAN_DIGEST: a64bd7e15bf434706bb89c00331d28e47843b437111371ecac8bb4f4fe8f8e37
                     PLAN: 	StreamAgg_11      	root	1	funcs:sum(tpcc.bmsql_order_line.ol_amount)->Column#12

	  └─IndexLookUp_18	root	0
	    ├─IndexScan_16	cop 	0	table:bmsql_order_line, index:PRIMARY(ol_w_id, ol_d_id, ol_o_id, ol_number), range:[1 7 2257,1 7 2257], keep order:false

```
 Plan 2:

```sql
	  └─IndexLookUp_25	root	8.674700015189103
	    ├─IndexScan_23	cop 	8.674700015189103	table:bmsql_order_line, index:PRIMARY(ol_w_id, ol_d_id, ol_o_id, ol_number), range:[1 6 2463,1 6 2463], keep order:false
```

review_comments: Why we don't reach this line if it's normalized?

Because `p.rangeInfo` maybe contain exact range information, such as:

```sql
IndexScan_16	... table:bmsql_stock, index:PRIMARY(s_w_id, s_i_id), range: decided by [eq(tpcc.bmsql_stock.s_i_id, tpcc.bmsql_order_line.ol_i_id) eq(tpcc.bmsql_stock.s_w_id, 1)], keep order:true
```

compare to

```sql
IndexScan_16 ... table:bmsql_stock, index:PRIMARY(s_w_id, s_i_id), range: decided by [eq(tpcc.bmsql_stock.s_i_id, tpcc.bmsql_order_line.ol_i_id) eq(tpcc.bmsql_stock.s_w_id, 2)], keep order:true
```
